seven_domain_review.finding: The draft fulfills the requested fresh complete scientific-body reading rather than treating an abstract or the old partial checkpoint as completion. It distinguishes workflow-call processing (first authorization or reuse) from request transport and remote settlement/return (IV.A/B, V.B/C, A.H-K). A reused copied call advances branch progress and can stale an edit although authorization-log bytes do not change. No conflation with end-to-end tool success found.

The empty frozen human guide and unique SYSTEM-99 Plan 56 remain constraints, not sources of inferred new implementation permission. The draft leaves all production changes, new ledgers/policies/enumerators, automatic restores/retries and directory migration unimplemented. The source reading does not reopen checkpoint-FD repair plan 1/1 revise or any older finite gate; no whole-batch completion is asserted.

The draft states the demanding finite registration and TCB premises: indexed finite pomsets and prefix-free completions, protected signed result authority and immutable call/action/request/source correspondence, domain disjointness, full tool mediation and restart-atomic linearizable transactions. CheckReg is restricted to finite-state source workflows with finitely many projected result-reaching tool traces; result-reaching tool SCCs are rejected while internal tau divergence may be erased. This cannot certify arbitrary unbounded LLM behavior or be supplied by a JSON digest/prompt alone.

Frozen search has 346 scanned entries, 25 missing-record errors, partial=false but status=incomplete and no hits: the draft correctly avoids claiming exhaustive absence or reusable validation. Conformal-policy-control, DPO and Frank-Wolfe knowledge hits do not establish exact execution-edit checking; no knowledge ref is adopted. Five c72 CI successes are historical configured-suite observations only, not evidence for paper proofs, full tool mediation, performance or model-task quality.

The scientific core is correctly represented. Indexed results are complete workflow alternatives rather than tool values or ResultStore records. StillRequired/Satisfied/AuthorizedRemoval is an exact partition with removals signed by original authority; only RestoreReplace treats completed current results as Satisfied. Table I has six typed edits, including choice versus parallel forks, replacement versus live restoration, selection versus join merge. Clone preserves underlying action sharing, causal order and authority while refreshing call/result identities; carried regions retain identity/progress. The safe family retains a completion for EACH compatible indexed result at EVERY admitted prefix. The yx/xz two-round cascade and nonempty greatest fixed point accurately distinguish jointly enforceable maximal behavior from per-result existence, one-pass pruning or plain DAG checks. Rejection certificates require exact synchronous removal batches; residual rechecking is under fixed derived parameters and updated Delta.

Formal scope and runtime assumptions are accurately bounded. Lean is the author-reported finite linear-contract core; general pomset/source-preservation, omission witnesses and ideal/runtime bisimulation are paper proofs not locally built proofs. Whole-component omission witnesses do not establish every byte is indispensable. Ready re-derives the target and whole fixed point, binds progress/queue/versions and refreshes every remaining token atomically. Reuse and dispatch can stale candidates. Restart assumes recovery of complete linearized commits; divergence-insensitive weak bisimulation hides repeated silent work and proves no fairness, termination or eventual remote completion. SQLite FULL/BEGIN IMMEDIATE here only covers local state; core handler execution is outside that transaction and results commit later, with explicit idempotent-retry versus unknown nonidempotent-side-effect boundaries. This is an applicability gap, not a newly demonstrated defect or a paper-equivalence claim.

Reported author evaluation is small finite checker/fixture evidence: 19 paper-specific tests plus 62 supporting regressions, accepted 2-128-result 0.11-53.47 ms, rejected 0.11-5.51 ms and 6-720-completion enumeration 0.33-50.35 ms. Fresh CPython 3.12 processes, median five repetitions and 16-vCPU AMD EPYC 7R12 are accurately stated. Output-sensitive complexity includes explicit emitted linearizations and compatibility triples and is not polynomial in compact concurrent workflows. No matched baseline, dispersion/CI, real-service crash race, provider task quality or full cost acceptance is supplied. One manual review only was used, with no tests, experiments, backend or old-gate retries.
